title: Aspiring writer-director here. I’ve got a question.

commenti.body:
1) easy enough to film, very engaging, opportunities for good times along with the bad, probably the most diverse of the three as there is a lot you can do with it. As a director, its gotta be quite high, as a viewer, it depends what you did with it exactly and what kind of balance between drama/comedy/emotional was struck. 8/10

2) I’m not sure what the impact would be other than “my classmate is a weirdo online” unless it had darker real-life implications. Hard to say really. 5/10

3) would depend on the ‘truth’ she discovers and how engaging it was along the way, could see it being a good film but unless it would need to either be spelled out to the viewers in a very obvious story pathway, or possibly be left to the interpretation of the viewer as to the final outcome of her story which would almost be better imho - definitely has potential but would possibly be a lot more difficult to articulate the poems into the script and may be more difficult to film. 6/10.

Not really one to give ranks, but i do have thoughts and some questions on these.

1. I'm kind of hesitant about this one. Portraying mental disorders accurately, and it sounds like the entire movie kinda centers around that. That might be a challenge for someone that is still green.

2. I'm interested, but it kinda sounds low-stakes. What exactly makes this tangible? Does the game bleed out into the real world?

3. I think this is the strongest, though I am not exactly poetry-savvy. Is this something where you would need to know the poems already, or would things be conveyed through settings and tones?
